Style material and typography:
exceptionally refined THIN frosted glass with convincing transparency and delicately lit edges.  Use the same selected background palette across all three creativity levels. Creativity changes the graphic expression, not the background color. Do not introduce gray or a smoky cast. Keep the thin-edge highlights, shadow contrast and glass translucency distinct even with this lighter background. Keep it smooth and uncluttered, with no grain, mottling, fog or decorative dot patterns.

The broad glass faces are highly transmissive, with a very light neutral frost rather than milky white fill. The background color and any small content-related forms behind them remain clearly visible, gently softened by diffusion. A few small forms may partly cross behind an edge: the exposed part is crisp, the covered part remains visible but softly blurred. Keep all such forms secondary to text, without large objects or a scene. Frost means soft light transmission, not coarse surface texture.

CRITICAL MATERIAL DETAIL: the glass must feel like an extremely thin tangible surface, not a flat white UI rectangle. Use one coherent soft upper-left light source. Each edge has a fine bright highlight on the light-facing side, a delicate cooler dark edge on the opposite side, and a tiny soft shadow immediately outside it. Let highlight intensity change naturally around the corners. This bright/dark pairing gives the perimeter subtle physical presence while the center stays clear and light. Do not draw a uniform white stroke around every side. A minute edge thickness is desirable; thick rims, heavy bevels, chunky acrylic, bulky side walls and liquid lens distortions are not. Keep shadows clean and restrained, never muddy.

Flat crisp Chinese geometric sans typography sits on the glass, untouched by background blur. Title is independent, flat bold the selected dark main color with a short warm-accent rule. Preserve precise alignment, elegant spacing and understated small icons. Creativity level 1 remains text-led; material craftsmanship can be excellent without increasing graphic complexity. No unrelated stars, ornamental quotation marks, dot matrices or repeated decorative icons. Let the full text determine the layout. This palette is the current test choice, not a universal rule.

palettes.name: 偏冷
palettes.prompt: Black-blue cold palette, not violet-blue: a clean luminous pale ice-white backdrop #EFF4F7 with a very subtle true-blue undertone. Opaque nearly-black ink navy #0B1E2B for the title, headings and body text. Deep midnight blue #17384D is the primary chromatic identity on selected meaningful icons, graphic details and precise glass edge reflections; restrained steel blue #416C85 supports it, with a small amount of pale icy blue #B4DEEB for airy cool highlights. The coldness comes from crisp black-blue depth against the light clear glass, not from purple, bright royal-blue saturation or darkening the whole slide. Make the dark blue details visibly present but keep their total area limited so the text stays dominant. Glass bodies and broad faces remain optically transparent and mostly colorless, transmitting the light background; only fine edges, localized refraction and selected semantic details carry the black-blue color. Preserve delicate bright/dark edge contrast without metallic rims or smoky gray slabs. Title underline uses steel blue or icy blue, overriding the generic warm-accent wording in the material block. No violet, purple, lavender, periwinkle, magenta, coral, orange or yellow. No all-over blue filter, dark backdrop, neon, dirty gray haze or black opaque glass.

palettes.name: 基准中线
palettes.prompt: The original reference palette for this glass style: very pale clean cool-blue background #EAF3FA; opaque deep midnight-blue typography #12314D; cyan #20B6CF as the key accent, with restrained cobalt #356EEA supporting glints and meaningful icon details. Glass remains mostly colorless or very subtly cool-tinted, transmitting the light background. This style's reference midpoint is naturally cool; do not neutralize it into black-white-gray. Use cyan for the short title underline, as in this original reference palette; this palette-specific title color overrides the generic warm-accent color wording in the material block. Keep the backdrop clean without a smoky gray cast. No added warm accent is required in this original palette.

palettes.name: 偏暖
palettes.prompt: Very pale clean warm ivory backdrop #F6F0E6; opaque deep blue-teal text #153E50. Glass bodies remain optically clear/colorless with only a trace of warm ambient transmission, not yellow amber blocks. Fresh lake-teal #58A8B1 remains a substantial cool supporting accent on graphic lines and icon details, balanced by warm apricot-coral #E49A74 on selected semantic details, key numerals and the title rule. Keep blue-teal and warm apricot both visible. Warmer RELATIVE to the original ice-blue palette, not absolutely orange or brown. No sepia wash, yellow light, brown text, gold metal trim or metallic objects.
